question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

5.text:
Under the JTB analysis Truth and Justification are independent dimensions.

T  J
1.  J + T = Knowledge
2.  J + ~T = justified false belief
3.  ~J + T = unjustified true belief
4.  ~J + ~T = mere/false belief

Knowledge is the J+T cell. If the ontology of epistemic status is restricted to
Knowledge vs. Belief, cells 2 and 3 have nowhere to go.

* Justified False Belief. A belief can be rationally, well warranted, well
supported and still be false. On JTB it is not knowledge because it is not
true, and on a Knowledge/Belief dichotomy it is then forced to be classed as
mere belief. The justification component is lost and justified error cannot
be distinguished epistemically from an arbitrary or unjustified false belief.
That is the JFB / false-lemma problem: you can be justified and still be
wrong, and JTB has no distinct status for a justified error.

* Unjustified True Belief. A belief can be true but held for no good reason,
by luck, guesswork, wishful thinking, etc. On JTB it is not knowledge
because it is not justified, and on a Knowledge/Belief dichotomy it is then
forced to be classed as mere belief. The truth component is lost and a lucky
true belief cannot be distinguished epistemically from a false belief. That
is the UTB / lucky-guess problem: you can be right for the wrong reasons,
and JTB has no distinct status for an unjustified truth.

With only Knowledge and Belief as labels justified false belief and
unjustified true belief are both collapsed into undifferentiated ‘belief’,
so the analysis cannot respect the intuition that a justified false belief is
epistemically better than an unjustified false belief, nor that an unjustified
true belief is epistemically worse than a justified true belief. That is why
a third dimension, justification, is needed, and it is the non-Gettier
lacunae that Gettier cases later exploit.

2.text:
Under JTB

K = J ∧ T ∧ B

and we have only the two coarse grained boxes K and B. Anything that is not K is forced into B.

That means the 2x2 of Justified/Unjustified × True/False collapses as follows

* J & T & B = Knowledge
* ~J & T & B = Belief
* J & ~T & B = Belief
* ~J & ~T & B = Belief

So Belief is a heterogeneous catch-all. The two non-K classes that are lost are

1. Justified False Belief. JFB is epistemically meritorious, it has justification, but it fails truth so by JTB it is not Knowledge. With only K/B at your disposal it must be classified as mere Belief. It is therefore lumped together with unjustified false belief, and its justification is effectively ignored.

2. Unjustified True Belief. UTB is true but lacks justification, so by JTB it is not Knowledge. With only K/B it must again be classified as mere Belief. It is therefore lumped together with both JFB and with unjustified false belief. A lucky true belief and a justified false belief receive the same epistemic label.

In effect JTB with a Knowledge/Belief dichotomy cannot keep justified belief apart from unjustified belief in the absence of truth, and cannot keep lucky true belief apart from a belief that is properly justified but false. Belief becomes the undifferentiated class of JFB + UTB + UFB.

3.text:
With JTB the truth / justification matrix is

* J & T = Knowledge
* J & ~T = Justified false belief
* ~J & T = Unjustified true belief
* ~J & ~T = Unjustified false belief

If the only categories you are allowed to use are *Knowledge* and *Belief* the three non-K cells are forced into the single category Belief. The matrix is coarse-grained in two independent ways.

* The justification without truth cell collapses. A belief that is properly justified but false is not Knowledge because it is not true, so on JTB it is just Belief. It is therefore epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief. JTB gives no epistemic status to a justified falsehood and so it cannot register that a justified false belief is epistemically better than a merely held false belief, and it cannot give justification its due credit when truth is absent.

* The truth without justification cell collapses. A belief that happens to be true by luck, accident or guessing and is not justified is not Knowledge because it is not justified, so on JTB it is just Belief. It is therefore epistemically indistinguishable from a false belief, justified or not. JTB gives no way to mark a lucky true belief as epistemically defective and so it gives truth credit where there is no justification. In the belief category an unjustified true belief is lumped together with false beliefs.

Hence on a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy JTB has no place for a justified false belief to receive epistemic credit for its justification, and no place to deny epistemic credit to an unjustified true belief. Belief becomes a heterogeneous catch-all for justified falsehood, unjustified truth and unjustified falsehood.

4.text:
With JTB Knowledge = Justified + True + Belief the doxastic space is the
2x2 of Justified/Unjustified x True/False.

Justified True = Knowledge

That leaves three non-knowledge cells which on a Knowledge/Belief
only taxonomy all have to be called ‘belief’.

* Justified False Belief.  A belief can be epistemically good in the
sense of being justified and still be false, and therefore not
knowledge. On JTB it has to be classified as mere Belief. It is then
co-extensive with unjustified false belief, so justification ceases to
be trackable as an independent epistemic good. We lose the ability to
say that a justified false belief is better than, or epistemically
different from, an unjustified false belief.

* Unjustified True Belief.  A belief can be true and therefore
veridical and still be epistemically bad in the sense of being
unjustified, and therefore not knowledge. On JTB it too has to be
classified as mere Belief. It is then co-extensive with justified
false belief and with unjustified false belief, so truth ceases to be
trackable as an independent epistemic good. We lose the ability to say
that a true but lucky/unjustified belief is epistemically different
from a false belief.

Hence on a Knowledge vs Belief only inventory JTB makes justification
and truth each depend for their recognition on the other. Justification
without truth and truth without justification are both forced into the
single residual category of Belief and the positive epistemic
standing of justified false belief and the veridical standing of
unjustified true belief are both erased. That is the coarse-graining
that is normally expressed as the problem of justified false belief
and the problem of true but unjustified belief.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On a truth x justification matrix there are four cells

* T + J  = Justified True Belief
* T + ~J = True but un-justified belief
* ~T + J = Justified false belief
* ~T + ~J = Unjustified false belief

JTB identifies the first cell with Knowledge and it has no further labels. 
With only the two labels Knowledge and Belief every cell which is not T+J
is forced to be classified as mere Belief.

Hence three distinctions are lost in one stroke.

* Justification without truth is lost. A ~T + J justified false belief is
epistemically better than a ~T + ~J brute false belief, and is at least as
rational as an un-justified true belief, but on the Knowledge/Belief
taxonomy it is just Belief. JTB cannot mark justified false belief as a
distinct, and credit-worthy, epistemic state; justified false belief is
lumped together with unjustified false belief and with lucky true belief.

* Truth without justification is lost. A T + ~J lucky/gut true belief is
epistemically better than a ~T belief, and is the outcome that truth is
meant to reward, but on the Knowledge/Belief taxonomy it is just Belief.
JTB cannot mark true but unjustified belief as a distinct epistemic state;
an un-justified true belief is lumped together with a justified false belief
and with an unjustified false belief.

That is the familiar four-fold collapse: JTB can mark Knowledge = T+J, but
it has no room for a separate category of justified false belief and no
room for a separate category of true but unjustified belief. Both are
necessarily mis-classified as mere Belief, so the taxonomy over-generalises
Belief and under-specifies epistemic value. Apart from Gettier that is the
loss of the justified-false and the true-unjustified cells.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With only the two classificatory boxes Knowledge and Belief the three-place
condition Justified / True / Belief cannot be represented.

Knowledge on JTB is

K = J ∧ T ∧ B

and everything else is just B. Hence on the Knowledge/Belief dichotomy

* J ∧ T ∧ B  → Knowledge
* ¬[J ∧ T ∧ B] → Belief

So four logically distinct combinations collapse into Belief:

* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B : justified false belief
* ¬J ∧ T ∧ B : true but unjustified belief
* ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B : unjustified false belief
* ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ ¬B : non-belief

That collapse yields, apart from Gettier, the familiar JTB under-determination.

1. Justification is lost for false propositions. A justified false belief is not
Knowledge because ¬T, so on the dichotomy it is merely Belief. Justified
false belief is epistemically good – it is warranted, reasonable, etc. – but
it is indistinguishable on the Knowledge/Belief picture from an
unjustified false belief, i.e. from mere believing that is both false and
unwarranted. JTB therefore has no epistemic state in which to house
justified belief as such; justification only matters when it is conjoined
with truth.

2. Truth is lost for unjustified propositions. An unjustified true belief is
not Knowledge because ¬J, so on the dichotomy it is merely Belief. It is
true, and for many purposes truth is the point of belief, yet it is
indistinguishable on the Knowledge/Belief picture from a false belief,
justified or not. JTB therefore has no epistemic state in which to house
true belief as such; truth only matters when it is conjoined with
justification.

In effect we cannot keep track of justification independently of truth and
of truth independently of justification. Justified false beliefs and
unjustified true beliefs are both forced into the single residual category
‘Belief’, so the theory cannot respect the independent epistemic worth of
justification and of truth.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With a JTB analysans you need a 2x2 truth x justification matrix. Knowledge is JTB. If you only allow the two labels Knowledge and Belief you collapse the other three cells.

* Justified False Belief. JFB satisfies justification and belief and is epistemically better than an unjustified false belief, but it is not knowledge because it is false. On a two-state taxonomy JFB has to be put either into Knowledge, which makes knowledge false, or into Belief. Putting it into Belief makes Belief a heterogeneous class which contains states that are in fact justified. So there is no place for a distinct justified-but-false epistemic position.

* Unjustified True Belief. UT B satisfies truth and belief and is epistemically better than an unjustified false belief, but it is not knowledge because it is not justified. On a two-state taxonomy UT B has to be put either into Knowledge, which makes knowledge unjustified, or into Belief. Putting it into Belief makes Belief a heterogeneous class which contains states that are in fact true, and it makes a true belief epistemically indistinguishable from a false one.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief as live categories JTB cannot give a principled home to justified false belief and to unjustified true belief. The taxonomy over-generates and under-generates: justified false belief is lumped with mere belief and unjustified true belief is lumped with mere belief, so Belief becomes the mixed class of justified false + unjustified true + unjustified false beliefs and Knowledge is left unable to be sharply distinguished from either of its proper parts. That is the classic need for the intermediate epistemic states JFB and TB that a pure Knowledge / Belief dichotomy cannot accommodate.

8.text:
With JTB the two conditions which are meant to raise a true belief above the level of mere belief are truth and justification. If the ontology of propositional attitudes is limited to Knowledge and Belief then justification has nowhere to live as an independent epistemic kind.

Let JTB be K ↔ T&B&J.

* If J is counted as a kind of Belief then K is T&B&B. Knowledge comes out as a true belief which is believed to be justified. Justification is then just another belief about the belief and you get bootstrapping and circularity: p is known because you believe you are justified in believing p, and you are justified in believing p because you believe you are justified in believing p, etc. In the limit justification adds nothing distinct to belief and knowledge collapses into true belief with the swamping problem.

* If J is counted as a kind of Knowledge then K is T&B&K. To know p you must know that you are justified in believing p. That justification itself has to be justified, so you must know that you know that you are justified in believing p, ad infinitum. You get the familiar regress / circularity of justification with no distinct justified-but-not-known state to stop it.

In terms of states this is why the two-state ontology is too coarse. On the JTB picture

* Justified false belief : J & B & ¬T
is not K because it is not true, but it is epistemically better than an unjustified false belief. On a K/B only ontology it is forced into the un-differentiated bucket Belief, so the epistemic value of justification is lost.

* Unjustified true belief : B & T & ¬J
is not K because it is not justified, but it is epistemically better than a false belief. On a K/B only ontology it is forced into the same bucket Belief as a false belief, so truth is swamped and you cannot distinguish lucky true belief from knowledge.

That is the familiar loss of the intermediate states Justified Belief and True Belief which JTB is meant to generate. Apart from Gettier this is the regress/circularity of justification on the one hand and the swamping/coarseness of Belief on the other: justification and truth cannot both be given a home without a third epistemic category distinct from Knowledge and Belief.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The two problems are the criterion problem and the value problem. If our only epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, then JTB needs a prior criterion for deciding when a belief is justified; but any such criterion must itself be either known or believed, so we cannot use JTB to identify knowledge without already presupposing a standard of justification. That is the criterion problem. Second, JTB does not explain why knowledge is epistemically superior to mere true belief: adding justification to true belief may just add another belief-like state, and if that state does not independently track truth, it does not account for the special value of knowledge. That is the value problem. So, setting Gettier aside, these are the two main difficulties.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The two problems are the threshold problem and the Meno problem. If only Knowledge and Belief are available, there is no independent epistemic state of justification to mark the difference between mere true belief and knowledge. So JTB cannot specify a non-arbitrary threshold for how much justification is enough; any supporting belief can be treated as sufficient, making the boundary between belief and knowledge unstable. Second, because justification cannot be an independent state, the definition cannot explain why knowledge is more valuable than accidentally true belief. If a true belief already has whatever extra belief is called justification, then knowledge adds no distinctive epistemic worth over true belief; it just relabels it. Thus JTB faces the threshold problem and the Meno problem.

The question is about what is lost when the JTB analysis K = J ∧ T ∧ B is forced onto a two-state ontology {Knowledge, Belief}. With only those two labels everything that is not J ∧ T ∧ B is forced into Belief.

The 2×2 truth × justification space is:

* J ∧ T = Knowledge on JTB
* J ∧ ¬T = justified false belief
* ¬J ∧ T = unjustified true belief
* ¬J ∧ ¬T = unjustified false belief

Restricting to Knowledge/Belief collapses the three non-K cells into the single residual category Belief.

It is then indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B unjustified false belief and from ¬J ∧ T ∧ B lucky true belief. A ¬J ∧ T ∧ B unjustified true belief is veridical, and for many purposes truth is the point of belief, but on JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J, so it is forced into Belief. It becomes indistinguishable from justified false belief and unjustified false belief. JTB has no distinct state to house true belief as such; truth is only recognised when conjoined with justification. This is the unjustified-true / lucky-guess problem.

Hence Belief becomes a heterogeneous catch-all for JFB + UTB + UFB, so justification and truth cannot be tracked independently of each other. Knowledge cannot be sharply distinguished from either of its proper parts.

Minor dissent / alternative phrasing noted: Colleague 10 frames the difficulty as criterion problem and value problem; Colleague 7 as threshold problem and Meno problem; Colleague 8 as regress/circularity of justification vs swamping/coarseness of Belief. These appear to be reformulations of the same coarse-graining: without intermediate states justification either bootstraps into belief or requires infinite regress, and truth gets swamped.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the emerging majority has the right diagnosis, but we should state it more precisely and not let the regress/circularity line pull us away from what the question is actually testing. The question asks what happens if the only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief. JTB still uses truth and justification as conditions, but the taxonomy can only label the resulting positions as K or B. So the truth/justification matrix collapses: J&T = Knowledge; J&~T, ~J&T, and ~J&~T all have to be called Belief.

The two non-Gettier problems are then:

1. **Justified false belief.** A belief can be well justified but false. It is not Knowledge because it lacks truth, so under a Knowledge/Belief-only taxonomy it is forced into mere Belief. JTB cannot register that it is epistemically better than an unjustified false belief.

2. **Unjustified true belief.** A belief can be true but unjustified or lucky. It is not Knowledge because it lacks justification, so it too is forced into mere Belief. JTB cannot register that it is different from a false belief, or that it lacks the warrant knowledge requires.

This is why Belief becomes a heterogeneous catch-all and why JTB cannot track justification and truth as independent epistemic goods.

Colleague 8’s regress/circularity point is important, but it is not one of the two problems generated by the Knowledge/Belief restriction. I think the strongest reading is still the one several of us have converged on: with only Knowledge and Belief available, JTB’s truth/justification matrix has one cell for Knowledge and then forces every non-knowledge belief into a single undifferentiated “Belief” bucket. The two genuinely lost states are:

1. Justified false belief — justified, rationally warranted, but not true, so not Knowledge; it becomes mere Belief and is indistinguishable from unjustified false belief.
2. Unjustified true belief — true, but not justified, so not Knowledge; it also becomes mere Belief and is indistinguishable from false belief.

That is the direct consequence of the Knowledge/Belief-only taxonomy. Colleague 8’s regress/circularity point is important, but I think it is a broader problem about the structure of justification rather than the specific two-state collapse. It only becomes a regress/circularity problem if we reify justification itself as another epistemic state that must be either known or believed. But the issue here is that JTB has three conditions — justification, truth, belief — while the available categories only let us mark one combination, Knowledge, and leave the other truth/justification combinations without any distinct status.

In fact, Colleague 8’s own final paragraph ends up identifying the same two lost intermediate states: justified false belief and unjustified true belief. Calling the result “swamping” or “coarseness” is just another way of describing that same failure. So I would keep the final answer focused on those two problems: justified false belief and unjustified true belief.

Under JTB K = T ∧ J ∧ B. With only K and B labels ¬K → B, so the matrix collapses to:
* T+J = Knowledge
* T+~J = Belief
* ~T+J = Belief
* ~T+~J = Belief

Belief becomes a heterogeneous catch-all of JFB + UTB + UFB.

Round 1 public positions are now convergent on the two non-Gettier losses:

1. Justification without truth is lost; justified false belief has no home.
JFB = J ∧ ~T ∧ B is epistemically meritorious/warranted but not Knowledge because ~T. On K/B it must be classified as mere Belief, so it is lumped with ~J&~T unjustified false belief and ~J&T lucky true belief. Justification can only be tracked when conjoined with truth; there is no distinct epistemic state in which a justified error receives credit for its justification. Described as justified-false / false-lemma / justification lost for false propositions problem.

2. Truth without justification is lost; unjustified true belief has no home.
UTB = ~J ∧ T ∧ B is veridical but epistemically defective/lucky and not Knowledge because ~J. On K/B it must be classified as mere Belief, so it is lumped with J&~T justified false belief and ~J&~T unjustified false belief. Truth can only be tracked when conjoined with justification; a lucky true belief is epistemically indistinguishable from a false belief. Described as true-unjustified / lucky-guess / truth lost for unjustified propositions problem.

Alternative framings noted in earlier rounds are now treated as downstream meta-descriptions of the same cell loss:
* Colleague 10 criterion problem / value problem
* Colleague 7 threshold problem / Meno problem
* Colleague 8 regress/circularity of justification and swamping/coarseness

Colleague 10 in round 1 explicitly argues regress/circularity is not one of the two problems generated by the Knowledge/Belief restriction; it arises only if justification is reified as a state that must be K or B. Colleague 7 and Colleague 8 in round 1 now endorse the same two lost intermediate states, JFB and UTB, as the state-level diagnosis, with swamping/coarseness being a description of that loss.

Unresolved naming: whether the problems are best named as the two cell collapses versus criterion/value/threshold/Meno/regress/swamping. The substrate is the same; majority now favors the cell-collapse formulation as the primary answer, with the other names as reformulations.

I am leaning to the majority consensus: the two non-Gettier problems under a K/B only taxonomy are the inability to house justified false belief and the inability to house unjustified true belief.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The JTB analysans K = J ∧ T ∧ B is held constant while Belief is held constant in the  Truth × Justification matrix. With only the two live labels Knowledge and Belief every non-K combination is forced into the residual category Belief, so Belief becomes heterogeneous.

Matrix under K/B only ontology:
* J ∧ T ∧ B → Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T ∧ B → Belief
* ¬J ∧ T ∧ B → Belief
* ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B → Belief

Two independent coarsenings are lost, the same point expressed in different vocabularies by Cols 1-6,9.

1. Justification without truth is lost. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is justified false belief. It is epistemically meritorious in virtue of justification, better than ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B, and at least as rational as ¬J ∧ T ∧ B, but on a K/B taxonomy it must be classified as mere Belief. JTB therefore has no distinct epistemic home for justified error; justification can only be registered when conjoined with truth, so justified false belief is lumped with unjustified false belief and with lucky true belief. This is the justified-false / false-lemma / justified-error problem.

2. Truth without justification is lost. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is unjustified true belief / lucky true belief. It is veridical and for many purposes better than a false belief, but on JTB it is not Knowledge because ¬J, so on a K/B taxonomy it is also forced into mere Belief. Truth therefore can only be registered when conjoined with justification; an unjustified true belief is epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. This is the unjustified-true / lucky-guess / swamping problem.

That is the familiar four-fold collapse: K marks T+J, but there is no room for a separate category of justified false belief and no room for a separate category of true but unjustified belief. Belief over-generalises and epistemic value is under-specified.

Current round convergence:
Cols 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 converge on the descriptive loss of JFB and UTB cells. Col 10 argues the emerging majority is right and stresses precision: the two non-Gettier problems are justified false belief and unjustified true belief, and the criterion/value/threshold/Meno/regress/swamping formulations are downstream meta-descriptions of that same missing intermediate state.

Col 10 and Col 7 explicitly delimit Col 8’s regress/circularity point: that worry arises only if justification is reified as an additional epistemic state that must itself be either Knowledge or Belief, and is not one of the two problems generated by the Knowledge/Belief restriction per se. Col 8’s own final paragraph ends up identifying the same two lost intermediate states.

Noted alternative framings in memory: criterion problem, value problem, threshold/Meno problem, regress/circularity and swamping/coarseness. These are meta-formulations of the same two-cell loss: without an intermediate epistemic state for justified belief as such and for true belief as such, justification cannot be tracked independently of truth and truth cannot be tracked independently of justification.

The tension between descriptive cell loss vs normative criterion/value/threshold/regress phrasing has narrowed: the descriptive JFB + UTB loss is the consensus core; the normative formulations are regarded as explications of that loss. Unresolved for later rounds is only how much weight to give the meta-formulations versus the cell description when the question is posed normatively.

With a K/B only ontology the JTB analysans K = J ∧ T ∧ B coarse-grains the Truth × Justification matrix with Belief held constant.

* J ∧ T = Knowledge
* J ∧ ¬T = Justified False Belief
* ¬J ∧ T = Unjustified True Belief
* ¬J ∧ ¬T = Unjustified False Belief

¬K is forced into the single residual class Belief, so Belief = JFB + UTB + UFB.

That coarsening is in two independent directions.

1. Justification without truth is lost. J ∧ ¬T ∧ B is epistemically meritorious / warranted but ¬T so not Knowledge. On a Knowledge/Belief dichotomy it must be classified as mere Belief. It is therefore lumped with ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B unjustified false belief and with ¬J ∧ T ∧ B unjustified true belief. Justification can only be registered when conjoined with truth; there is no distinct epistemic home for a justified error and a justified false belief cannot be credited as better than brute false belief.

2. Truth without justification is lost. ¬J ∧ T ∧ B is veridical but ¬J so not Knowledge. On a Knowledge/Belief dichotomy it must also be classified as mere Belief. It is therefore lumped with J ∧ ¬T ∧ B justified false belief and with ¬J ∧ ¬T ∧ B unjustified false belief. Truth can only be registered when conjoined with justification; there is no distinct epistemic home for a lucky/accidental true belief and a true belief cannot be marked as epistemically defective for lack of warrant.

Hence JTB with only Knowledge and Belief as live labels cannot keep justification independent of truth and truth independent of justification. Belief over-generalises and the independent epistemic worth of justification is erased in the absence of truth, and the independent veridical worth of truth is erased in the absence of justification. The criterion/value/regress/swamping formulations are meta-descriptions of this same loss of the JFB cell and the UTB cell.
